_doc: AI data changes. Entry: {"sheet":"constant","id":"AI_Army_StuckTime","path":["value"],"expected":5,"value":4,"why":"..."}. 'expected' is checked against vanilla; path indexes into the row (e.g. ["values",3,"val"] = Insane).

changes.why: Vanilla re-rolls the retreat ratio every tick in [0.5,0.8], so any fight below ~0.8 retreats within a second (6 vs 8 armies always ran). Fixed 0.65; tools/behave.py multiplies the fight balance by the terrain factor (own land 1.3, enemy land 0.8) before the check.

Vanilla Defense (checkStructures) re-rolls its required ratio in [Min, Max] every 0.5 s (Insane 1.0-3.5): the same defense was refused 400-1600x and sent at random moments. Fixed 1.15 = ENTER 1.5 / own-zone terrain 1.3 (vanilla's estimate has no terrain factor): enter on our own land. Short of it, rules/rally.py gathers.
Medium too: the testbed's human-slot faction (Atreides, AI after P) reads the Medium values (its defense picks rolled 0.80-2.50)

User rule: always max out the army. Vanilla keeps a free-CP reserve by these goals (free CP = prod of the no-stock CommandPoint; low > high is inverted: >= low buys, <= high never, between only when Solari + Manpower are above goal): 25 of the base 40 CP held back at day 1, 5-10 at day 100, and past the last row (day 200) the reserve grows again with time. low 1 / high 0 for every AI type: recruit whenever a unit could fit (the recruit cost check includes the CP upkeep, so it never overshoots the cap); last row at day 100000 so the past-the-end scaling never applies. CP overflow from temporary units: tools/rules/army.py.

Vanilla adds upgradeFactor x this (only for factor > 1: a village bonus to the building's output, Upgrades.getUpgradeFactor) to a building's score: x3 gave a 1.5x Manpower village ~+4.5 for its Recruitment Office, less than a MissileBattery's map-exposure +5 / +9 (Harkonnen built one on Yedah). x10: villages build into their own bonus first (expert play), every faction and bonus kind.

Score added to a building related to a resource vanilla lists as under-producing (resource.aiRelatedBuildings, Manpower -> RecruitmentOffice). With the army always at full CP (CommandPoint prodGoals patch) Manpower is the recruitment bottleneck; 6 -> 12 pushes its building harder, likewise for any other short resource.

Vanilla's siege scan (getSiegeableVillages, closure f40784) drops every village within this many zones of a sandstorm (const >= zone distance). Storms barely touch ground armies (Storm_Army: speed x0.7, armor -3, regen -0.05, cloaked, no worm vibration; Fremen's Reduced variant only cloaks), so Annex / Pillage / Liberate targets vanished for no reason. -1: never excluded.

Supply Drop is the universal first operation (strategy ARMORY-OPS) but only the Military AI type weighted it. Weight 5 for every AI type (no aiType = all in HAI.getAiWeight). Vanilla never launches it (rules/sdrop.py sdrop-block); our rule casts it for a far siege / raid or a stranded army.
